name: Toast
layerWhy: It reports one outcome where the person can no longer see it; it is a voice of other parts, not a job.
promise: Something just happened out of sight, and it can be undone for a moment.
expectation: A short message in the corner that fades, with Undo when there is one.
evidence: It stays five seconds, eight with an action, waits while pointed at or focused, and announces itself politely.
behaviour: At most three; a newer one pushes the oldest out.
Its action closes it after running.
It sits above dialogs (a manual popover).
context: The outcome of an action whose place is gone, or of work that finished elsewhere. Never routine outcomes, lasting facts, questions or errors to fix.
relationships: Its place is "toast" in the behaviour model.
It holds the undo of a reversible destructive action.
accessibility: A labelled region with a polite live region.
Its buttons are real buttons in the tab order.
failures: Never the only place an error shows.
Never takes an undo away while it is being read.
dont: A toast for a saved setting.
